title: Nagrand
body: Nagrand is one of the few green lands left on shattered Draenor. While the rest of the world was scorched by fel magic or torn apart, these rolling grasslands survived largely untouched, and great islands of earth still drift above the plains, spilling waterfalls into the lakes below. For the orcs, Oshu'gun, the diamond mountain in the southwest, was once the heart of their faith: the clans gathered beneath it each spring, and their shaman spoke there with the ancestors. Now the land is crowded with peoples and dangers. The Mag'har, orcs who never drank the demon's blood, hold Garadar in the north, while the Kurenai, Broken draenei who seek redemption, have reclaimed Telaar in the south. Between them the abandoned draenei city of Halaa changes hands in open war. Warmaul and Boulderfist ogres fight over the hills, the Shadow Council lurks at Kil'sorrow Fortress, the Burning Legion builds forge camps in the west, and at the Throne of the Elements the Earthen Ring struggles to calm the restless spirits of the land.

title: Garadar
body: Garadar, the home of the Mag'har, stands in northern Nagrand. Its people call themselves survivors of the red pox and of a shattered world, and because they were set apart from the rest of their race, they never shared the corruption that turned other orcs green. Today Garadar is a town under strain. Refugees from Sunspring Post and the Bleeding Hollow village crowd its streets with orphaned children, the matrons struggle to feed them, and the Greatmother lies ill in her hospice while young Garrosh broods by the fire. Captain Kroghan, a Horde officer sent only to pass through, has chosen to stay on as the Horde's liaison to the town.

title: Telaar
body: In the far south of Nagrand lies Telaar, one of the very few draenei towns on Draenor whose graceful architecture survived intact. It is home now to the Kurenai, a tribe of Broken who escaped their slavers and work to overcome their demonic taint; their name means redeemed. They took the town back only recently and mean to keep it. Arechron leads them, with Mo'mor the Breaker, Otonbu the Sage and Poli'lukluk the Wiser at his side. They have welcomed the Alliance their draenei kin have joined. In the town's jail, blood elves captured at Halaa await questioning, and the old hatred between the Broken and the orcs is never far from anyone's mind.

title: Halaa
body: On a plateau in the heart of Nagrand stand the empty halls of Halaa, once the foremost draenei research site for the study of naaru crystals. Its builders are long gone, but their notes on the crystals of Oshu'gun remain, and powder from the diamond mountain is found in the earth all across the region. That prize has drawn the Alliance and the Horde into open war. Draenei and blood elves fight over the town street by street, and whichever side holds it brings in researchers to gather the crystal powder, quartermasters to reward their soldiers, and guards to defend the walls until the next assault. Rarely does a banner fly over Halaa for long.

title: Halaani Basin and the Twin Clefts
body: Below the plateau of Halaa spreads the Halaani Basin, a wide hollow where Nagrand's troubled waters gather. Spawns of muck crawl through its pools, and the Earthen Ring warns that each leaves tainted debris that will spread unless carried away. Enraged crushers, hulking elementals of living rock, roam the basin as well. Within it lie the twin clefts, Northwind and Southwind, where Boulderfist shock troops have hidden their ogre mounds. The ogres stacked supplies stolen from the Bleeding Hollow village in the clefts, and when young Corki of Telaar went looking for trouble, it was here that the Boulderfist caught and caged him.

title: The Throne of the Elements
body: In the northern hills beyond Skysong Lake rises the Throne of the Elements, a sacred place where the spirits of Nagrand are honored. The four furies dwell there in person: Gordawg of earth, Incineratus of fire, Aborius of water and Kalandrios of air. Shaman of the Earthen Ring keep the site, among them Elementalist Sharvak, who fears for a world whose people fight on while the elements themselves are in turmoil. Some of her companions are Broken, such as Morgh and Lo'ap, elementalists of the Ring like herself. Envoys of the Ring travel to both Garadar and Telaar to report on the state of the elements.

title: Skysong Lake
body: Skysong Lake lies just below the Throne of the Elements, and its waters are in turmoil. A disturbance in the ebb and flow of the region's waters has driven the lake spirits into a frenzy, and they have begun to wreak havoc through the waterways. The shaman of the Throne say that Watoosun of the Water came to them in a vision and allowed them to put the maddened spirits down, on the condition that the cause of the trouble also be found. Talbuk graze along its shores, and the great crocolisk Goretooth hunts the lakes of Nagrand.

title: Windyreed Village
body: Windyreed Village, a cluster of huts southeast of the Throne of the Elements, is home to the Windyreed, a tribe of Lost Ones. The Lost Ones are draenei who have fallen even further than the Broken, a people once banished to the swamps of Zangarmarsh, and the scavengers and wretches who go about the huts bear every mark of that fall. They have come a long way from the marsh to settle here.

parts.body: The shaman of the Throne name the village as one source of the sickness in Nagrand's waters. The Lost Ones, they say, mean to carry their corruption out of the marshes and into these lands, and the Earthen Ring has sought the counsel of the furies on how to answer them.

parts.body: The furies answered with fire. Flame drawn from Incineratus himself was set loose among the huts to show the Lost Ones the wrath of the elements, and it checked the spread of their pollution, though other troubles soon surfaced. Lo'ap, ashamed, owned that the villagers were his own kin, dredging up Nagrand's waters to make marsh.

title: Sunspring Post
body: Sunspring Post was a Mag'har fishing village on the shore of Lake Sunspring, the only holding the orcs of Garadar kept outside their walls. It fell to a raid by the Murkblood, a tribe of Broken who serve the bog lord Musel'ek of Coilfang. The orcs who lived there were slain or driven out, and the Murkblood dumped the bodies into the lake, threatening the water that Telaar also drinks. Now Murkblood raiders and putrifiers prowl the empty huts, bending the spirits of the air to their will and troubling the lake with their magic as they search for something hidden there.

parts.body: Something worse lurks in the depths of the lake. When Watoosun of the Water shed the stink of corruption, the filth took on a life of its own: a polluted spirit made of the vilest stuff found among the elements, which now hides in Lake Sunspring and breeds corrupt offspring.

title: The Ancestral Grounds
body: Far to the southwest of Garadar lie the Ancestral Grounds, where the Mag'har carry their dead to be laid among the honored spirits. It is the domain of Mother Kashur, a spirit of the ancestors who dwells there still. The grounds were always a quiet, undisturbed place, but of late the ancestral spirits have risen in great agitation, wandering the hills in torment. A funeral procession bound here from Garadar some days ago has not arrived.

parts.body: The procession will never arrive. On the road from Garadar the Warmaul surrounded it, cut down its guards and most of its mourners, and defiled the body of the elder being carried to rest, for no reason but to show what they could do.

title: Oshu'gun
body: Oshu'gun, the diamond mountain, towers over southwestern Nagrand, a vast crystal glittering above the plains. For the orcs it was the heart of their faith: every spring the clans gathered here for a great festival, and their shaman communed with the ancestors in its shadow, until the clans became a horde and the spirits fell silent. Its crystals draw covetous eyes. The Consortium wants to mine it, rogue ethereals are already prying fragments loose, and Shadow Council ritualists and Legion terrorguard have crept inside.

parts.body: The mountain is not stone at all. It is the wreck of the vessel that first carried the draenei across the stars, which came down out of the sky and crashed here in an age long past, and within it, trapped in the wreckage, lingers the naaru K'ure, whose weakened energies have never escaped.

title: The Spirit Fields
body: The Spirit Fields spread around the foot of Oshu'gun, and the name has never been more fitting. Ancient orc ancestors drift across the grass toward the mountain, murmuring of pain and a cold embrace, drawn by a pull they cannot resist. Voidspawn wander among them, and rogue ethereals of the Vir'aani pick at the mountain's fallen crystals. The land is perilous in other ways. The gronn Durn the Hungerer circles the fields hunting anything that moves, and the great clefthoof Banthar leads her herd here.

parts.body: Of late, strange dark distortions have begun to appear in the air over the Spirit Fields. They cannot be seen with the naked eye, but a gnomish inventor insists that readings from them are vital to the campaign at the Sunwell, and volunteers are sent out from Shattrath with special goggles to take them.

title: Aeris Landing
body: North of Oshu'gun, the ethereal traders of the Consortium have set up camp at Aeris Landing. Their ground operations leader, Gezhe, spent months planning to mine Oshu'gun, which he calls the largest diamond known in the universe, only to be told by Nexus-Prince Haramad to wait until a political matter in Netherstorm was settled and not to anger the naaru. In the meantime Gezhe runs a clearing house for smuggled gems and pays well for ogre warbeads of obsidian. His security officer Zerid complains that the camp sits barely ten feet from crazed voidspawn, and the merchant Shadrek quietly buys elekk ivory, insisting it is not poaching.

title: Kil'sorrow Fortress
body: Kil'sorrow Fortress is a walled orc stronghold in southeastern Nagrand near the Terokkar border, named for the demon lord Kil'jaeden. Its masters, the Kil'sorrow, are agents of the Shadow Council who still commune with the Burning Legion. Cultists, spellbinders and deathsworn warriors patrol its walls alongside dark worgs, and its ritualists have spread to Oshu'gun. Garadar and Telaar both post bounties for Giselda the Crone and her lackeys, wanted for murder, ritual sacrifice, kidnapping, burglary and communing with the Legion.

parts.body: Of late the fortress has found a new enemy. Warmaul banners turned up driven through the hearts of slain Kil'sorrow, and the bodies of Kil'sorrow soldiers were laid out in the Laughing Skull Ruins as if after a great battle, until the Kil'sorrow and the Warmaul ogres were at war. It was all a ruse by Lantresor of the Blade.

title: Burning Blade Ruins
body: East of Telaar, near the Terokkar border, the Burning Blade Ruins hold the largest gathering of Boulderfist ogres in southern Nagrand. Great pyres burn on the upper levels of the compound. From here the ogres have struck at their neighbors: Bleeding Hollow orcs were driven from their village in a night attack, and the Kurenai fear that the ogre hunting parties now ranging toward Telaar are the forerunners of an invasion.

parts.body: The Boulderfist did not come here by choice. A new clan of ogres, the Warmaul, has taken their lands to the north and is driving them ever further south, and the Boulderfist have turned in desperation on the orcs and Broken in their path.

title: Laughing Skull Ruins
body: Against the northern mountains of Nagrand lie the Laughing Skull Ruins, one of the old villages of the orc ancestors. The Warmaul ogres have overrun it and built an ogre mound among its broken walls. From here Zorbo the Advisor and his reavers and shaman have planned attack after attack on Garadar and Telaar, slaying orcs and Broken alike, and both towns pay for proof of his death. A blazing pyre lights the ruins' courtyard. The most famous corner of the ruins, though, is the Ring of Blood, where the goblin Gurgthock stages fights for the ogres' amusement.

parts.body: The courtyard pyre once served a darker purpose. At a smoke signal sent up beside it, Boulderfist ogres crept in and laid out the bodies of slain Kil'sorrow orcs around the fire, so that the Warmaul would believe a great battle had been fought there and turn on the Kil'sorrow.

title: Warmaul Hill
body: In the northwestern mountains of Nagrand stands Warmaul Hill, stronghold of the Warmaul ogres. Its great cave once belonged to the gronn who ruled these ogres, until Cho'war the Pillager drove them out and named himself king. The Warmaul are cruel even by ogre standards. They keep captured Mag'har in cages to be eaten fresh, their chef stirs a bubbling stew and boasts of his Broken chowder, and they hoard supplies stolen from a Kurenai caravan. Mountain gronn still roam the slopes.

parts.body: The hill hides a darker secret. Somewhere on its slopes the ogres worship Gurok, an earth spirit who betrayed the elements, at an earthen brand of stone, and Gordawg of the Throne of the Elements says that seven Warmaul skulls laid upon it will call the usurper out.

title: The Forge Camps
body: In the far west of Nagrand the Burning Legion has raised two forge camps, Hate and Fear, to build weapons for its war on this land. Each camp has a forge, spell warding towers and a transporter linking it to the Legion's armies, and as long as the transporters stand nothing done to the camps will last. Mo'arg engineers and tinkerers labor beneath the watch of felguard and the fel cannons of the camp defenses. A mo'arg master planner keeps the blueprints that decide where every structure goes, and each camp is ruled by a pit lord overseer, Demos at Hate and Xirkos at Fear, so dangerous that Altruis warns any who would face them to bring allies.

title: Nesingwary Safari
body: On the northeastern edge of Nagrand, near the border of Zangarmarsh, the famous dwarf hunter Hemet Nesingwary has pitched his camp. He came to Outland in search of real big game, and he has the scars to prove he found it. With him are Shado Farstrider, a quiet hunter who earned the nickname Fitz by losing a wager to Hemet over a frostsaber in Winterspring, and Harold Lane, who insists that the infected scratch he got brawling with a talbuk stag and a pair of windrocs is nothing. Their pilot, Marsha, is patching up the flying machine that crashed because Hemet shot through its ailerons. A copy of Hemet's book, The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, lies in the camp.

title: The Ring of Trials
body: The Ring of Trials is the great arena of Nagrand, and the old battlemaster Garokk remembers when it was a place of great glory and honor. Then the Steamwheedle Cartel arrived with wagons of gold and pens sharper than any axe. The goblins took the arena over and renamed it Steamwheedle Stadium, and it now hosts the bouts of the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit. The organizer King Dond sells the charters that would-be gladiators need, while the brute Ear-Biter turns away anyone he judges unworthy of the ring. Garokk lingers nearby, a battlemaster without a battle.

title: The Twilight Ridge
body: High on the Twilight Ridge of western Nagrand, reached only on wings, stands a dimensional gateway through which the Burning Legion once brought demons into this world. The gateway is dark now, but not forgotten. Deathshadow cultists have built a camp around it, and Shadow Council spellcasters channel magic into its frame in an effort to stabilize it and open the way again. They are overseen by the eredar Reth'hedron the Subduer, whose own brother, Balthas, is a lord in Illidan's service. Illidan's forces strike at the ridge whenever they can, determined that the portal stay closed.

title: Greatmother Geyah
body: Greatmother Geyah is the venerable matriarch and spiritual leader of the Mag'har. In a very real sense she raised every orc in Garadar: most were too young or too sick to remember the Dark Portal, many of them orphans, kept apart from the healthy as Blackhand willed, and she nursed them back to health. The town's matrons dread the day she passes. That day seems close: she has fallen gravely ill and keeps to the hospice, while the clan's young war chief sinks into despair, calling her the balance that holds back his father's blood lust. Yet her mind is sharp, and she still guides those who would help her people.

parts.body: Geyah is the mother of Durotan, the Frostwolf chieftain who left Draenor long ago with his mate Draka and gave his life so that later generations might be born free of the blood curse. Draka was carrying a child when they left, and Geyah secretly begged the spirits to protect it. When word came that Durotan's son had survived and now leads the Horde, she wept, and begged to see her grandchild before she leaves this world.

title: Garrosh
body: Garrosh, son of Grommash Hellscream, is the young war chief of the Mag'har and heir to lead them when the Greatmother passes. He carries that duty like a curse. He has grown up in the shadow of his father's name, for the blood lust that consumed Grom Hellscream is said to have cursed their people, and Garrosh fears the same rage waits in his own veins. With Geyah dying and enemies on every side, he sits by the fire in Garadar, unmoved by victories and deaf to calls for action, while Jorin Deadeye openly calls him an impotent whelp.

parts.body: Even the news that the ancestors could rest did not move him. His people were proud, he granted, proud to see one more winter, but he could see nothing beyond it. The stranger should lead the clan, he said, so that he could die when the Greatmother passed and be free of his family's shame. His cursed blood ran too deep; he would not be the second Hellscream to bring ruin on the orcs.

title: Jorin Deadeye
body: Jorin Deadeye, son of Kilrogg, calls himself the last of the line of Deadeye, warchiefs of the Bleeding Hollow clan, and he names the Mag'har proudly as survivors: of a fallen dynasty, of the red pox and of a shattered world. When Boulderfist ogres fell on his village by night and drove his people out, he escaped to Garadar and found its leader weeping into a fire. Jorin has little patience for that. He believes ogres respect only might, and he sends every willing warrior to teach them so.

parts.body: Yet he is shrewd as well as fierce. When his scout sent word that the Boulderfist answered to one of their own race, an ancient orc returned from Azeroth, Jorin chose to send an envoy to him before an army, to ask that the ogres be pulled back.

title: Saurfang the Younger
body: Saurfang the Younger was one of the Garadar younglings who could bear no more after yet another Murkblood raid and set out to strike back, though their elders tried to stop them. The war party, barely grown, took the western road toward Sunspring Post and was cut to pieces. Alone left alive, he tells of a rage that burned through his whole being as thirty Murkblood closed around him, and of waking later with no memory of the fight, eyes still flashing red. Nearly dead, he was found by the survivors of a funeral procession, and now he burns for vengeance.

parts.body: He will not go home. Saurfang believes his destiny lies elsewhere, that he will serve a greater purpose someday, and he sent word to Farseer Corhuk that he must walk the earth. Corhuk only nodded and wiped away a tear. The son is the father, he said, and may the spirits have mercy on those who stand in his way.

title: Arechron
body: Arechron leads the Kurenai of Telaar, and he carries the weight of his people with a weary dignity. Murkblood raiders and Boulderfist ogres press on a town the Kurenai have only recently taken back. His greatest trial, though, is his son Corki, a boy whose curiosity keeps leading him into trouble. Even from inside an ogre cage, Corki assures his rescuers that his father, the leader of Telaar, will reward them handsomely, and Arechron can only sigh that the boy will be the death of him.

parts.body: He knows his enemies personally. The Murkblood invasion plans that reached him were in a hand he knew: Ortor, a Broken who was once noble and wise in the ways of the elements and is now a muck addled lackey of Musel'ek the bog lord, and Arechron cursed him for a traitor.

title: Lantresor of the Blade
body: Lantresor of the Blade is an old orc blademaster who makes his home on a high platform of the Burning Blade Ruins, in the midst of the Boulderfist ogres. To a stranger's eye he looks every inch an orc. He greets those who come before him by asking who so boldly stands there and whether they do not know death by sight, and he is as cunning as he is deadly.

parts.body: He is not wholly an orc. Lantresor is a blademaster of half orc and half draenei descent, one of a rare breed nearly all killed decades ago. He crossed the Dark Portal with the Horde in the days of the first invasions, served under two Warchiefs and returned to Draenor, and now he rules the Boulderfist. Pressed by the Warmaul and harried by orcs and Kurenai alike, he offered the envoy who came to him a bargain: help him turn his enemies against one another, and his ogres would leave their people in peace.

title: Altruis the Sufferer
body: Altruis the Sufferer is a night elf demon hunter who came to Outland in Illidan's service and left it. He still honors Illidan for setting him on his path, but believes his old master has become the very thing he swore to fight, and he counts the Illidari as foul as any demon. He rode into Nagrand on Nethrandamus, his nether drake, asked questions in Garadar and Telaar and let it be known that seekers of a purpose would find one with him. His camp in the west looks out over the Legion's forge camps. His name is feared in the Legion's fields, and the Aldor and the Scryers send their agents to him for knowledge of Illidan's demon hunters.

title: K'ure
body: Deep within Oshu'gun dwells K'ure, a naaru whose voice is a gentle melody in the mind. The Consortium has been ordered to stay out of the mountain for fear of angering a powerful naaru, and Gezhe's people grumble that they must wait while the Sha'tar finish whatever business they have inside. Around the mountain, orc ancestors drift toward Oshu'gun as if something within were calling them.

parts.body: Oshu'gun is his ancient vessel, the ship that first brought the draenei to this world. It fell from the heavens and crashed here many hundreds of years ago, and his weakened energies have been trapped in the wreckage ever since. He admits that he is the source of the ancestors' pain.
sources: quest 10101 reward text (ancient vessel, ship that first brought the draenei, crashed many hundreds of years ago, source of the orc spirits' pain)

parts.body: As his Light bled away over the centuries, a void grew in its place and began to devour the souls of those nearby, and generations of orc spirits have been drawn helplessly into it. Worse, the Burning Legion has learned to harness the vortex and draw void creatures into its armies. K'ure believes the key to ending the cycle lies with another naaru, A'dal of Shattrath.

title: Cho'war the Pillager
body: Cho'war the Pillager holds the deepest caves of Warmaul Hill, in the northwestern mountains of Nagrand, and the Warmaul ogres of the hill answer to him. The way to him runs past cages of captives, heaps of stolen goods and a great many of his warriors, for he is never left unguarded, and those who reach him find a huge and brutal ogre ready to fight for his cave.

parts.body: In Garadar his rise is told as a rumor. The ogres of the hills once served the gronn, until Cho'war drove the gronn out of their cave on Warmaul Hill, declared himself king and dissolved the clans that had served under them. From those pieces the Warmaul were born. It was his ogres who ambushed a Mag'har funeral procession, and the Mag'har want his head.

title: Durn the Hungerer
body: Durn the Hungerer is a gronn, one of the sons of Gruul, the great gronn lord whose lair lies in the Blade's Edge Mountains. Durn has claimed the Spirit Fields around Oshu'gun as his hunting ground. He circles the mountain without rest, destroying everything in his path. He is huge and merciless even by the measure of his kind, and anyone who crosses the fields near the diamond mountain may find the gronn bearing down on them.

parts.body: Both Garadar and Telaar have put a price on his head, the last and greatest of the bounties their wardens offer, for none has yet been able to rid Nagrand of him. Those who take up the hunt are urged to gather their allies before they go.

title: The Fall of Sunspring Post
body: When the Murkblood Broken sacked Sunspring Post, slaying or driving out every orc who lived there, both of Nagrand's towns felt the blow. In Garadar, the farseers of the Lightning Sons refuse to sit idle while their chieftain grieves: one seeks the Murkblood's twisted idols, another their leader's head. In Telaar, the Kurenai fear for the lake. Otonbu the Sage wants the rotting bodies of the dead burned before they poison the water, knowing the orcs will never understand, and Poli'lukluk sends fighters to thin the raiders, for all an orc sees is Broken. At the Throne of the Elements, the Earthen Ring has learned that the raiders are capturing spirits of the air.

parts.body: The raiders are planning more than raids. Crudely painted maps of Nagrand carried by the Murkblood bear a big red mark where a town should be, and those who find them carry the plans home in haste: the Broken are preparing an attack.

parts.body: The farseer got his wish. The raiders' leader, Ortor of Murkblood, was slain among the huts of Sunspring, and his head was set upon a pike outside the gates of Garadar, a warning to any who would think to attack the town again.

parts.body: The hand behind the plans was one Arechron knew: Ortor of Murkblood, once his friend and a noble Broken versed in the ways of the elements, now a muck addled servant of the bog lord Musel'ek. Ortor fell at Sunspring, but Arechron wonders what could have driven the Murkblood to so audacious an advance into orc lands. There is more to this, he says, than meets the eye.

title: The Missing Procession
body: Though the Greatmother lies ill, she insists that life must go on, that her people must serve as an example to Garrosh, and so a funeral procession of Mag'har set out from Garadar for the Ancestral Grounds. Funeral rites are sacred to the Mag'har. Several days later the procession has still not returned. Matron Drakia, with so many other matters to attend to, asks a stranger to follow the western road out of Garadar, keep clear of Halaa, and search for the missing mourners.

parts.body: Of the thirty who set out, only two elders were found alive, Yorley and Ungriz. Warmaul ogres had fallen on the procession from all sides, slaughtering guards and mourners and desecrating the remains of the elder they were carrying, purely to show their power. Even the gentle Yorley, a spiritual orc, wanted vengeance on Warmaul Hill.

title: Lantresor's Gambit
body: The Boulderfist ogres are on the move. In Garadar, Jorin Deadeye, driven from his village in a night attack, sends help to his scout Kilrath, who hides by the ruined Bleeding Hollow village over the Terokkar border watching the ogres and their fat leader. In Telaar, the huntress Bintook spots an ogre hunting party far from its mound, and the Kurenai fear it is the first sign of an invasion. Both towns mean to answer with blood at the Burning Blade Ruins and the twin clefts of the Halaani Basin, but neither yet knows who leads the Boulderfist, or why they have come south.

parts.body: On Kilrath's plan the fat ogre, Unkor, was beaten until he talked. A new clan, the Warmaul, was driving the Boulderfist from their lands and killing their people; the Boulderfist chieftain, Krol, had vanished, and one Lantresor of the Blade ruled in his place. Jorin was far from pleased to hear that his village had been destroyed because the ogres needed more space.

The Warmaul had kicked the Boulderfist out of their mounds to the north, and with so many more mouths to feed, the hungry ogres had come looking for food, little Broken included.

With his two enemies at each other's throats, Lantresor sent a peace offering home with the envoy: his clan had been saved from extermination, and the Boulderfist would accept peace.

title: Gurok the Usurper
body: At the Throne of the Elements, Elementalist Untrag feels something pounding beneath the earth, endlessly, as if to punish it, and sends a stranger to hear the earth fury Gordawg. Gordawg speaks little. He chews rocks to learn where they have been, and he knows that something from the underneath is forcing the elements out. First he sets the stranger to lay the tortured earth spirits of the Telaari Basin back to sleep, then to break the raging crushers that roam Nagrand and bring him their pieces to taste.

parts.body: Gordawg chewed the crushers' cores and spat them out, pelting the stranger with rubble. Poison, he said. These rocks are not of Nagrand; they come from poison, and destroying the poison rock would lead to the usurper behind it.

title: The Polluted Waters
body: Elementalist Lo'ap of the Earthen Ring can see that Nagrand's waters are sick. Before sending anyone into them, he prepares tablets from a rare bean, picked from the dung of the plains' beasts, that let a body breathe water as if it were air. The maddened water spirits of Skysong Lake must be put down first, with the permission of Watoosun of the Water, who has granted it on one condition: that the source of the disturbance be found as well. Beneath Halaa, meanwhile, spawns of muck must be slain and their tainted cores carried away so that the poison spreads no further.

parts.body: The source proved to be the Lost Ones of Windyreed Village, who mean to spread their filth beyond the swamps of Zangarmarsh. With the blessing of the furies, Lo'ap handed over living fire plucked from the fiery essence of Incineratus himself, to be unleashed upon the village's huts.

title: The Ring of Blood
body: In the Laughing Skull Ruins the Warmaul ogres keep a fighting pit, the Ring of Blood, and the goblin Gurgthock runs its bouts, with his troll servant Wodin at hand. The rules are simple: the fight ends when one side lies dead on the arena floor. A challenger's first opponent is Brokentoe, a ferocious clefthoof, and from there the fights only grow harder, on the road to a bout with the Warmaul champion. Mogor, hero of the Warmaul, watches every fight and scoffs at the winners while the ogres' bets climb. Gurgthock, of course, bets on the challenger.

parts.body: The road to the champion was long. After Brokentoe came the Murkblood twins known as the Blue Brothers, then Rokdar the Sundered Lord, a giant hard as rock hauled from Blade's Edge, then Skra'gath, a creature of air and shadow. The Warmaul champion himself had to be shipped in from the gladiator pits of Blade's Edge, where he trained against mountain giants three at a time.

title: Altruis and the Forge Camps
body: When Altruis the Sufferer arrived in western Nagrand, he left word in Garadar and Telaar that any who sought a purpose should come to him. He is a hunter of demons, and once he could sense a demon from a thousand paces, but the Legion has put wards around its forge camps to the west that hide them from his sight. So he sends his volunteers soaring over the camps on the back of his nether drake, Nethrandamus, to note every structure and every defense, so that a counterattack can be planned.

parts.body: Slowing the camps' engineers bought him time, but as long as the transporters stood nothing would last, and fel steel could not be destroyed by ordinary means. Altruis wanted the camps' blueprints, stolen from their mo'arg master planner, and he sent them to an old acquaintance in the Lower City of Shattrath: Sal'salabim, a drunken mo'arg who had once been a Legion engineer.

parts.body: After some persuading, and a few debts collected, Sal'salabim laughed and gave his answer. The camps were his own design, and their warding towers blind a demon hunter's eyes. Turn the camps' own fel cannons around, he said. The catch was that only the pit lord overseers held the keys to turn them.

title: The Restless Ancestors
body: Sent for by the Greatmother through a grudging Garrosh, a stranger comes before Greatmother Geyah. Mother Kashur, a spirit of the Ancestral Grounds, wishes to speak with them, and to make that possible Geyah sends the stranger across Outland for four herbs: Olemba root from Terokkar, marshberries from Zangarmarsh, Telaari fronds from Nagrand and dragonspine from the Blade's Edge Mountains. From them she brews a potion meant to expand the mind, so that the stranger may see the spirits and speak with them.

parts.body: The potion, Kashur later admitted, did nothing; a spirit can be seen only if it allows it, and the potion was a test of belief. The ancestors at the Grounds had risen in torment, and when the stranger visited the old villages of the ancestors, Sunspring, the Laughing Skull Ruins, Garadar and the Bleeding Hollow, no spirits were at home. All were drifting south.

parts.body: Kashur sent the stranger on to Oshu'gun, where the naaru K'ure revealed the truth: the void growing in his failing vessel was swallowing orc souls. He advised the stranger to seek out another naaru, A'dal, in the city of Shattrath.

parts.body: A'dal sent the stranger into the Auchenai Crypts, where the spirit of another naaru, D'ore, explained that the cycle could not be stopped, only eased, for without the void the Light cannot exist. Using the crypt's soul mirrors, the stranger freed the ancient spirits of Nagrand before the void could claim them, and Mother Kashur gave thanks beyond words.

title: Hero of the Mag'har
body: The ancestors can rest at last, and the Greatmother hopes the news will lift even the young Hellscream from his malaise. Garrosh, son of Grom, has sat by the fire through every victory won for the Mag'har, sure that his cursed blood makes him unfit to lead. So Geyah sends the stranger who has done so much for her people to Garrosh himself, to tell him of their latest victory and to say that all of it was done for him and for his people.

parts.body: It did not work. Garrosh admitted that his people were proud, but asked what lay beyond another winter, offered to let the stranger lead the clan instead, and declared that he would never become the second Hellscream to damn the orcs. Too ashamed to face the Greatmother, he sent the stranger back to tell her.

parts.body: In tears, Geyah sent the stranger across the Dark Portal to Orgrimmar with a message for the Warchief: his blood is here, on this shattered world, and his father's legacy endures. Tell him everything, she said, and tell him that she awaits him here.

parts.body: Thrall answered. He came to Garadar with the Doomhammer, and the Greatmother, her eyes failing, knew her grandson by the way he moved and gave him at last the name Durotan had meant for his son: Go'el. Learning how Grom had truly died, she begged Thrall to tell Garrosh as well, and when he had, Garrosh cast off the shame of his bloodline and took up his father's name as chieftain of the Mag'har.

title: The Nagrand Safari
body: Hemet Nesingwary does not let just anyone hunt with his expedition, and in Nagrand the tests are harder than ever. Hemet starts his recruits on the clefthoof near camp, then the far more dangerous bulls, and finally Banthar, the fiercest and hairiest clefthoof in Outland, who roams with her herd near Oshu'gun. Fitz Farstrider, who speaks of honoring the last heartbeats of fallen prey, leads hunters through ever deadlier windrocs to their mother, Gutripper, far to the west. Harold Lane, too sick from his scratch to hunt, sends others after talbuk stags, thorngrazers and Bach'lor, king of the stags.

parts.body: Those who master all three hunts may face the queen of Nagrand: Tusker, a giant elekk who stands on a great bluff above Oshu'gun, beside whom Bach'lor, Gutripper and Banthar are nothing. Hemet offers, only half in jest, to send a letter to the next of kin.
